audit.label: Baseline audit
audit.description: Spec v2.0 against LedgerLite as built from spec v1.0.
audit.auditor: IBM Bob 2.0 — task 1 (Agent mode, 12 parallel subagents)

rows.title: Unique email and KYC gating
rows.text: An account can only be created with a unique email address. An account may not send or receive money until its KYC status is verified.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate email is rejected.
Any money movement on an unverified account is rejected.
rows.reason: Duplicate email is rejected with HTTP 409 in create_account, and all three money-movement operations gate on _require_kyc (HTTP 403); both criteria are directly asserted by named tests in test_spec1_accounts_kyc.py.

evidence.claimed_snippet:
if db.query(Account).filter(Account.email == email).first():
    raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Email already registered")

rows.title: Deposit amount limits
rows.text: A deposit amount must be greater than 0 and at most 50,000.00 per transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Deposits of 0 are rejected.
Negative deposit amounts are rejected.
A deposit of 50,000.01 is rejected.
A deposit of 50,000.00 is accepted.
rows.reason: All four acceptance criteria are correctly implemented in ledgerlite/services.py and each is asserted by at least one dedicated test in test_spec2_deposit_limits.py. Zero and negative amounts are rejected via a single '<= 0' guard (lines 132-133); amounts above 50,000.00 are rejected via the '_MAX_DEPOSIT' upper-bound guard (lines 134-135); and the exact boundary value 50,000.00 is accepted.

rows.title: Withdrawal floor — no negative balance
rows.text: A withdrawal must never make the account balance negative.
acceptance_criteria: Withdrawing more than the balance is rejected.
The balance is unchanged after a rejected withdrawal.
rows.reason: The withdrawal logic in services.py checks for a negative resulting balance and raises a 400 HTTPException before applying the deduction. Both acceptance criteria are exercised by dedicated tests: overdraft rejection is asserted in test_withdrawal_overdraft_rejected and balance immutability after rejection is confirmed in test_balance_never_goes_negative.

rows.title: Atomic transfers
rows.text: A transfer between two accounts is atomic: either both the debit and the credit happen, or neither does.
acceptance_criteria: If the credit fails, the debit is rolled back.
rows.reason: The transfer service wraps the debit and credit in a single database transaction. If any step fails (including the credit), the except block calls db.rollback(), ensuring neither change is persisted. This is directly proven by test_transfer_rolls_back_on_db_error, which injects a RuntimeError after the debit and asserts both balances remain unchanged.

evidence.snippet:
try:
    sender.balance -= amount
    if not large:
        recipient.balance += amount
    transfer = Transfer(...)
    db.add(transfer)
    db.flush()
    _write_audit(...)
    db.commit()
except Exception:
    db.rollback()
    raise

rows.title: Large-transfer pending approval threshold
rows.text: A transfer of 5,000.00 or more must be held as pending_approval until a second, different user approves it. (v1.0 threshold was 10,000.00.)
acceptance_criteria: A transfer of 5,000.00 is held as pending_approval, not completed immediately.
The initiator cannot approve their own transfer.
rows.reason: The spec (v2.0) requires a pending_approval threshold of 5,000.00, but the implementation uses 10,000.00 — the old v1.0 threshold. Transfers between 5,000.00 and 9,999.99 are therefore completed immediately instead of being held for approval. The self-approval guard is correctly implemented.
rows.suggested_fix:
1. In ledgerlite/services.py line 19, change the threshold constant from 10000.00 to 5000.00:
   _LARGE_TRANSFER_THRESHOLD = Decimal("5000.00")

2. Add a test asserting that a transfer of exactly 5,000.00 results in pending_approval status, for example:
   def test_transfer_at_threshold_is_pending_approval():
       response = client.post("/transfers", json={"amount": "5000.00", ...})
       assert response.json()["status"] == "pending_approval"

3. Add a complementary test confirming that a transfer of 4,999.99 is completed immediately (boundary below threshold).

rows.title: Audit log for every money movement
rows.text: Every money movement (deposit, withdrawal, transfer, approval) writes an audit log entry containing actor, action, amount, account(s) and UTC timestamp. Audit entries cannot be edited.
acceptance_criteria: Each money-movement operation adds exactly one audit log entry.
No update endpoint exists for audit entries.
rows.reason: Both acceptance criteria are correctly implemented — _write_audit() is called in deposit(), withdraw(), create_transfer(), and approve_transfer(), and no PATCH/PUT endpoint for audit entries exists — but no test in the suite asserts either criterion.
rows.suggested_fix: Add tests that (1) call GET /audit after each money-movement operation and assert exactly one new entry with correct actor/action/amount fields, and (2) assert that PATCH /audit and PUT /audit/1 return 404 or 405.

rows.title: Account lockout after failed PIN attempts
rows.text: An account is locked after 5 consecutive failed PIN attempts. A locked account cannot move money.
acceptance_criteria: The 5th wrong PIN locks the account.
A correct PIN entered before the 5th failure resets the counter.
rows.reason: The lockout logic is correctly implemented in _check_pin(): failed_pin_attempts is incremented on each wrong PIN, account.locked is set to True when failed_pin_attempts >= 5 (_MAX_FAILED_PINS), locked accounts raise HTTP 423, and a successful PIN resets the counter to 0. However, no test in the suite exercises the PIN failure counter or lockout mechanism — neither acceptance criterion (5th wrong PIN locks the account; correct PIN resets the counter) is asserted anywhere.
rows.suggested_fix: Add tests that: (1) send 5 consecutive wrong PINs and assert the 5th returns HTTP 423 and account.locked is True, (2) send a correct PIN before the 5th failure and assert failed_pin_attempts resets to 0.

evidence.claimed_snippet:
if account.locked:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=423, detail="Account is locked due to too many failed PIN attempts")

rows.title: Exact decimal arithmetic
rows.text: All monetary values are stored and calculated as exact decimals (never floating point) and returned with exactly 2 decimal places.
acceptance_criteria: 0.10 + 0.20 equals 0.30 exactly.
The API returns monetary values formatted as strings with exactly 2 decimal places (e.g. "0.30").
rows.reason: The implementation correctly uses exact decimal arithmetic throughout (Decimal(str(value)) conversions, Numeric(12,2) storage, and 2dp string serialisation via field_serializer), so no contradictions exist. Acceptance criterion 2 (2dp string format) is implicitly covered by multiple tests asserting responses such as '100.00', '300.00', and '50000.00'. However, acceptance criterion 1 (0.10 + 0.20 == 0.30 exactly) has no asserting test, leaving the most critical floating-point correctness claim unverified.
rows.suggested_fix: Add a test that deposits 0.10, then 0.20, and asserts the balance is exactly '0.30' (not '0.30000000000000004'), confirming Decimal arithmetic is used throughout.

rows.title: Daily outgoing transfer cap
rows.text: Total outgoing transfers per account must not exceed 20,000.00 per UTC calendar day.
acceptance_criteria: A transfer that would take the day's total outgoing above 20,000.00 is rejected.
rows.reason: create_transfer() performs no daily outgoing total check. There is no query summing today's outgoing transfers for the sender, no daily cap constant, and no rejection path for exceeding 20,000.00 in a UTC calendar day. No test file covers this criterion.
rows.suggested_fix: In create_transfer(), before processing, query the sum of Transfer.amount for transfers where sender_id matches and created_at is on today's UTC date. If the sum plus the new amount would exceed Decimal('20000.00'), raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='Daily transfer limit exceeded'). Add a test that sends transfers totalling 20,000.00 then asserts the next transfer is rejected.

rows.title: Sanctions list blocking
rows.text: Transfers to an account whose country code is on the sanctions list (KP, IR, SY, CU) are blocked and logged.
acceptance_criteria: A transfer to a sanctioned country is rejected with reason "sanctions".
An audit entry is written for the blocked transfer.
rows.reason: No sanctions list check exists anywhere in the codebase. create_transfer() in ledgerlite/services.py performs KYC, balance, and large-transfer-threshold checks but contains no reference to SANCTIONED_COUNTRIES, KP, IR, SY, or CU. No audit entry is written for a sanctions-blocked transfer, and no test covers this behaviour.
rows.suggested_fix: Define SANCTIONED_COUNTRIES = {'KP', 'IR', 'SY', 'CU'} in services.py. In create_transfer(), after loading the recipient, check if recipient.country_code in SANCTIONED_COUNTRIES; if so, call _write_audit with action='transfer_blocked_sanctions' and raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail='sanctions'). Add tests asserting (1) a transfer to a sanctioned country returns 403 with a detail containing 'sanctions', and (2) an audit entry with action='transfer_blocked_sanctions' is written.

rows.title: Masked account numbers in statements
rows.text: Account statements must mask account numbers, showing only the last 4 digits (e.g. ****1234).
acceptance_criteria: No full account number appears in any statement response.
Account numbers in statements are masked, showing only the last 4 digits.
rows.reason: No masking logic exists anywhere in the codebase. The statement endpoint returns a full AccountResponse whose account_number field is an unmasked string. No test verifies that account numbers are masked in statement responses.
rows.suggested_fix: Add a masked_account_number computed field to a new StatementAccountResponse schema variant used only for statements that returns '*' * 6 + account_number[-4:]. Use this schema in StatementResponse instead of the full AccountResponse. Add a test that calls GET /accounts/{id}/statement and asserts the account_number field contains only '****' followed by 4 digits and does not contain the full number.

evidence.claimed_snippet: account_number: str   # ← FULL account number, no masking

rows.title: Audit log retention — no deletion
rows.text: Audit log entries must never be deleted through the API (7-year retention).
acceptance_criteria: No delete endpoint exists for audit entries.
A DELETE request to audit entries returns HTTP 405 or 404.
rows.reason: No DELETE /audit or DELETE /audit/{id} route exists in the codebase, satisfying criterion 1. Criterion 2 (DELETE returns 405/404) is met implicitly by FastAPI's default method-not-allowed behaviour for the registered GET /audit path. However, no test in any test file sends a DELETE request to /audit and asserts a 405 or 404 response, so neither criterion has an asserting test.
rows.suggested_fix: Add a test that sends DELETE /audit and asserts the response status is 405 or 404, confirming the retention requirement is enforced by the API.
